messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after the 02:00 runtime push we saw KV prefix hit-rate drop ~18% on the p99 traffic slice. GPU memory pressure spiked and two hosts hit OOM, autoscaler kicked in but latency climbed.

sam: saw the same in traces. p99 token latency +210ms, throughput steady. attaching quick flame: kernel-switch path shows more time in the fallback matmul kernel.

lee: curious — did anything change in key canonicalization? last week we moved to normalized prompt keys (strip whitespace + normalized placeholders). could be a key churn bug.

maria: i dug logs — there are a bunch of unique prefix keys with only 1-2 hits each post-deploy. before deploy we had long-tail with repeated keys. looks like canonicalization mismatch between the router and the prefiller.

sam: hypothesis: new batching heuristic extended sequence padding to nearest 64 tokens, increasing per-request seq_len variance. that reduces prefix reuse because kv-keys are now length-sensitive.

anya: to confirm, can we compare key hash distributions pre/post? i ran a quick sample: pre: top-1k keys accounted for 42% hits. post: top-1k down to 27%.

lee: that aligns. Also noticed our LRU softcap eviction sweep ran more frequently; fragmentation on GPU slabs increased free slots but not contiguous space -> allocation failures -> OOM.

maria: ops-bot noticed two nodes with slab fragmentation > 72% at 02:07. ops-bot: "Alert: gpu-slab-frag high on g-node-14" :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.02.18/runtime-v12 completed at 02:00 — change log: batching heuristic tweak, prompt-normalization refactor, kv-prefetch opt.

sam: action items: 1) revert normalization change on router to see if hit-rate returns 2) run canary with previous batching padding 3) instrument key hashing counts and TTL eviction counters per-slab.

lee: i'd add a short-term mitigation: reduce TTL from 1h -> 10m for GPU hot cache to reduce fragmentation amplification. also enable soft-evict probabilistic compaction to reclaim slots without full rewarm.

maria: started a canary: rolled back normalization on 2 hosts (g-node-2/3). watching metrics.

anya: while that runs, i'm preparing a heatmap of prefix hit re-use windows. propose we try a decay-window rewarm: when a key sees second hit within X seconds we mark as sticky for longer TTL; otherwise let it decay faster. Should reduce noise from single-shot keys.

sam: good idea — that sticky TTL can be heuristic: if hit_count > 3 in last 5m -> extend TTL *2. implement as config flag first.

maria: canary looks promising: g-node-2/3 show top-1k -> 40% again and p99 latency back to baseline on those nodes. non-canary still bad.

lee: for kernel selection: fallback matmul path is slower but more memory-efficient. if fragmentation causes big contiguous alloc failures, runtime is switching kernels and that increases latency. we should add a metric for kernel-fallthrough rate per-request.

maria: opened an issue + PR tracker: runtime#4589 — add per-kernel selection counter + expose slab fragmentation percent and failed-alloc events to console.

anya: experiments to run (short list): 
- A: full revert of normalization + canary observe (done)
- B: batching pad rollback to previous quantiles (small canary)
- C: sticky-ttl heuristic + soft-evict compaction (staging)
- D: proactive prefill for top-10k keys into GPU cache on restart to speed rewarm

sam: timeline: run B and C tomorrow morning low-traffic window, D as a resilience test after we stabilize.

lee: note about OOM avoidance: add retry path with small micro-batching (split into 2 smaller batches) when alloc fails instead of immediate fail; reduces tail latency impact.

maria: putting all experiment configs in the perf-playbooks repo and will post links. thanks all — will update once B/C are scheduled. :thumbsup:
